artworks.title: The Sleep of Endymion
artworks.description: Girodet's celebrated Neoclassical canvas, painted in Rome and exhibited at the Salon of 1793, shows the shepherd Endymion stretched out in a languid, almost weightless slumber while a beam of cool moonlight—the disembodied presence of his lover Selene—caresses his nude body. The winged figure of Zephyr parts the branches to admit the goddess's radiance, transforming the silvery light itself into the erotic protagonist. The dreamy androgyny of the sleeping youth and the diffuse luminism mark a deliberate break from David's severe classicism, making the work an early icon of pre-Romantic sensibility. It now hangs in the Louvre, Paris.

artworks.title: Selene and Endymion
artworks.description: In this exuberant Venetian Rococo composition, Sebastiano Ricci paints the moon goddess Selene descending through a luminous sky in her chariot to visit the sleeping Endymion, whose eternal youth and beauty Zeus has preserved in unending sleep. Putti and billowing drapery animate the heavens while the shepherd reclines below with his flock, his crook beside him, oblivious to the divine visitation. Ricci's airy palette and dynamic diagonal of swirling clouds capture the tender, recurring nocturnal union of immortal and mortal that lies at the heart of the myth.

artworks.title: Diana and Endymion
artworks.description: A pupil of Jacques-Louis David, Langlois renders the moment of the goddess's nocturnal descent with polished Neoclassical clarity. Diana—the Roman Luna, identified with Selene—leans tenderly over the sleeping Endymion, a crescent moon crowning her brow, while a winged Cupid draws back the veil of night to reveal the youth. The smooth modelling, restrained gestures, and idealized anatomy reflect the discipline of the Davidian school, and the chaste eroticism of the encounter is conveyed entirely through the goddess's lingering, downward gaze upon her perpetually dreaming beloved.

artworks.title: Selene and Endymion (wall painting from Pompeii)
artworks.description: Recovered from a house in Pompeii (insula VI 9, 6–7) and now in the National Archaeological Museum of Naples, this Roman fresco depicts the moon goddess Selene approaching the slumbering Endymion. The shepherd reclines in the relaxed pose that became the canonical formula for the myth across antiquity, while the goddess descends from above to gaze upon him. The painting attests to the popularity of the Endymion theme in domestic Roman decoration, where the image of beauty preserved in eternal sleep—forever visited by divine love—carried funerary as well as amorous resonance.

popCulture.title: Endymion
popCulture.creator: John Keats
popCulture.description: Keats' long romance opens with a thing of beauty and keeps the sleeping shepherd as Romantic poetry's favourite dreamer under the moon.

popCulture.title: Endymion, the Man in the Moon
popCulture.creator: John Lyly
popCulture.description: Lyly's court comedy borrows the shepherd's endless sleep for Elizabethan allegory — Endymion rapt before Cynthia, the moon-queen of Whitehall.

popCulture.title: Mamoru Chiba
popCulture.creator: Naoko Takeuchi
popCulture.description: Sailor Moon's Tuxedo Mask is Prince Endymion in a past life — the Latmian sleeper renamed as the moon princess's destined consort for a modern manga audience.
